sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: New patient visit. Generally well; mild fatigue after work. Menstrual tracking since January: bleeding 4-5 days, moderate first two days, mild cramps, cycles usually 27-31 days. Uses condoms; no pregnancy attempts yet. No intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding. Mostly vegetarian diet; no GI bleeding or blood donation.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 112/70 mmHg, pulse 72/min, weight 60.8 kg, height 165 cm. Heart and lungs normal. No pallor, thyroid enlargement or abdominal tenderness.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Routine preventive visit. Fatigue requires investigation; iron deficiency is suspected, not yet established. No known chronic illness, prior surgery or drug allergies. Does not smoke; alcohol 0-2 drinks weekly.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Request CBC, ferritin and TSH. Cervical screening appointment arranged for February. Review diet, activity and cycle tracking. Return earlier for worsening fatigue, bleeding or shortness of breath.

sections.heading: Laboratory comment
sections.text: Low ferritin supports depleted iron stores. Hemoglobin remains within the adult female reference interval. Interpret with clinical findings.

procedures.name: Speculum examination and cervical cytology collection

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Fatigue persists. No melena, rectal bleeding or abdominal pain. Dietary iron intake is low. Normal menstrual volume by history.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: Consent obtained for speculum examination; synthetic nurse Rena Elm present as chaperone. Cervix appears normal; no contact bleeding or abnormal discharge. Cervical sample collected.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Ferritin 11 ug/L and hemoglobin 124 g/L on January 21 confirm iron deficiency without anemia. Likely dietary and menstrual contribution; no evidence of a bleeding disorder.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Start ferrous sulfate 300 mg (60 mg elemental iron) every other day. Discuss constipation, nausea and separation from tea/calcium. Repeat CBC and ferritin after treatment. Cytology result pending.

documents.title: Iron results review and cervical examination

sections.heading: Specimen
sections.text: Liquid-based cervical sample; cervix source. Collected February 2. Satisfactory for evaluation, including transformation-zone component.

sections.heading: Interpretation
sections.text: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Screening result; a negative result does not exclude all cervical disease. Routine interval under the programme in effect at collection; earlier review if symptoms develop.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Mild nausea with morning iron; no vomiting or constipation. No new bleeding.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue the same 300 mg every-other-day dose, taken in the evening with food for tolerability. Recheck in May. Cervical cytology from February 7 is NILM; result communicated.

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Ferritin has increased from 11 ug/L on January 21. Hemoglobin is stable.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Energy improved. Completed alternate-day iron through August 1. No new menstrual or gastrointestinal symptoms.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Improved iron stores after treatment; May 20 ferritin 34 ug/L, hemoglobin 130 g/L. No anemia.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Stop therapeutic iron after completed course. Continue dietary iron. Repeat if fatigue recurs. Cycle tracking remains useful for menstrual health.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Plans to begin trying to conceive in January 2023. Cycles remain 27-31 days with 4-5 days of flow. Uses condoms until then. Started folic acid 400 micrograms daily on December 1. Childhood rubella and varicella vaccination documented in synthetic history.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: BP 110/68 mmHg; weight 61.0 kg. No new findings.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue folic acid, avoid alcohol while attempting pregnancy, review fertile-window timing and vaccination history. Influenza vaccine given with consent; no immediate reaction. Cervical screen February 2022 NILM.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Three days of sore throat, rhinorrhea and dry cough. No dyspnea or chest pain. Home COVID antigen negative, patient-reported.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Temperature 36.8 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air; chest clear, no tonsillar exudate.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Likely self-limited viral upper respiratory infection. Fluids and rest; return for persistent fever or breathing difficulty. No antibiotics. Continuing folic acid; pregnancy not documented.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Trying to conceive since January 1, 2023 with regular unprotected intercourse. No positive pregnancy tests. Cycle lengths 27-31 days; no hirsutism, galactorrhea, significant pelvic pain or dyspareunia. Partner is fictional Alex Chen, SYN-PARTNER-001; age 32, no known reproductive history.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Subfertility concern at about eight and a half months. Under age 35; infertility criteria not yet met. No documented PCOS or endometriosis.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Review timing and continue folic acid. Arrange assessment if no pregnancy after twelve months. Patient requests advance referral due to clinic wait; full evaluation to occur after January 2024.

sections.heading: Recipient
sections.text: Dr Neri Solan, Example Cedar Reproductive Centre

sections.heading: Reason for referral
sections.text: Dear Dr Solan: Please assess Maya Chen when she reaches twelve months of attempts in January 2024. She began trying January 1, 2023 and has no known pregnancy. This advance referral reflects waiting time, not a confirmed infertility diagnosis.

sections.heading: Relevant history
sections.text: Regular cycles 27-31 days, mild cramps, no pelvic surgery, STI/PID history or clinical hyperandrogenism. Cervical cytology February 2022 NILM. Iron deficiency without anemia treated in 2022; May hemoglobin 130 g/L and ferritin 34 ug/L.

sections.heading: Current management
sections.text: Folic acid 400 micrograms daily. No drug allergies. Please consider ovulatory, tubal and partner evaluation if conception has not occurred. Yours sincerely, Dr Elara Vale. Copy to patient.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Nurse intake for January physician assessment. No pregnancies to date, G0P0. Intercourse every 2-3 days since January. Last tracked start November 1; usual flow five days. No prior hormonal fertility medication.

sections.heading: Relevant negatives
sections.text: No dysmenorrhea requiring time off, intermenstrual bleeding, dyspareunia, galactorrhea or prior pelvic infection. Family history negative for early menopause. BMI 22.5 kg/m2 from weight 61.3 kg and height 165 cm.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Baseline endocrine bloods and pelvic ultrasound may be completed before the physician visit. Partner semen analysis requested separately with consent. Tubal testing will be scheduled following the physician assessment if still indicated.

sections.heading: Clinical context
sections.text: Cycle day 3, menstrual bleeding started November 28. AMH describes ovarian response potential and cannot establish the cause of infertility. No pregnancy established.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Baseline fertility evaluation; cycle day 4, LMP November 28. Consent documented for transvaginal imaging.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound. Chaperone Rena Elm.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Anteverted uterus 72 x 38 x 44 mm. Homogeneous myometrium, no focal lesion. Endometrium 4.2 mm, no cavity lesion. Right ovary 28 x 19 x 21 mm, AFC 8; left ovary 27 x 18 x 20 mm, AFC 7. Total AFC 15. No adnexal mass or free fluid.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: No structural abnormality identified. AFC 15. Ultrasound does not demonstrate tubal patency or exclude endometriosis.

sections.heading: Context
sections.text: Menstrual start November 28; urinary LH surge December 12 reported by patient. Sample obtained eight days after LH surge, approximately one week before expected next menses. Progesterone supports recent ovulation; one value cannot assess luteal quality.

sections.heading: Recipient
sections.text: Dr Elara Vale, Example Orchard Family Practice

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Dear Dr Vale: Maya has now attempted conception for over twelve months without pregnancy. Regular cycles and progesterone 38 nmol/L on December 20 support ovulation. Baseline ultrasound shows AFC 15 and no cavity lesion. AMH 18.6 pmol/L, FSH 6.2 IU/L, TSH 1.85 mIU/L. G0P0.

sections.heading: Partner context
sections.text: Partner assessment documented separately: semen concentration 48 million/mL, progressive motility 42%, morphology 5% on December 8, 2023, within that synthetic laboratory reference limits. These are partner facts, not Maya laboratory values.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Tubal patency remains unassessed, so unexplained infertility is provisional. Discuss expectant management, ovarian stimulation with IUI, and IVF. Continue folic acid. Arrange HSG early in a cycle after negative pregnancy test.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Infertility assessment. Cycle day 9, LMP January 24; urine pregnancy test negative today. No symptoms of pelvic infection. Risks explained and consent documented.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.text: Fluoroscopic contrast hysterosalpingography using 8 mL nonionic iodinated contrast. Examination tolerated with brief cramping.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Normal uterine cavity contour without filling defect. Both tubes opacify; free bilateral intraperitoneal spill. No hydrosalpinx.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: Bilateral tubal patency. No cavity abnormality identified. This study does not exclude pelvic endometriosis.

sections.heading: Recipient
sections.text: Dr Elara Vale

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: HSG February 1 confirms bilateral spill. Ovulatory pattern, unremarkable pelvic ultrasound and partner semen assessment support unexplained infertility. No confirmed PCOS, endometriosis or tubal obstruction.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Reviewed continued attempts, three to four cycles of oral ovarian stimulation with IUI as a usual first treatment, and IVF. Couple elects IVF after discussion of costs, injection burden, procedural risk and alternatives. They understand that response and live birth cannot be guaranteed. No IUI cycles undertaken.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: One antagonist stimulation cycle planned for June. Conventional IVF and freeze-all strategy selected, with elective single frozen embryo transfer after recovery. No PGT planned. Continue folic acid.

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Consent documented for infectious screening. Rubella IgG supports immunity; negative screens do not establish lifetime absence of infection.

sections.heading: Protocol
sections.text: Antagonist cycle, SYN-IVF-01. Start medications only after baseline clearance. Initial schedule is provisional; monitoring determines changes.

sections.heading: Prescription
sections.text: Follitropin alfa 225 IU SC nightly, planned June 2-10, quantity 2025 IU, no repeats. Menotropins 75 IU SC nightly June 2-10, nine vials, no repeats. Cetrorelix 0.25 mg SC daily when instructed, five prefilled syringes, no repeats. Leuprolide acetate 4 mg SC once at instructed trigger time, one dose, no repeats.

sections.heading: Counselling
sections.text: Injection teaching completed. Discussed OHSS symptoms, emergency contact, and medication reconciliation. No treatment started today.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Cycle day 2, LMP June 1. SYN-IVF-01 antagonist protocol.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Endometrium 3.8 mm. Right AFC 8 and left AFC 7; no ovarian cysts. Serum estradiol 112 pmol/L; progesterone 1.0 nmol/L; beta-hCG <1 IU/L.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Baseline cleared. Start follitropin alfa 225 IU SC and menotropins 75 IU SC nightly today. Monitoring June 7; cetrorelix not yet started.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.text: Transvaginal follicle tracking with consent. SYN-IVF-01.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Right follicles: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9 mm. Left: 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9 mm. Endometrium 7.4 mm, trilaminar. No free fluid. Mild bloating only; no dyspnea or oliguria.

sections.heading: Orders
sections.text: Estradiol 2480 pmol/L; progesterone 1.4 nmol/L. Reduce follitropin alfa from 225 to 150 IU nightly starting tonight. Continue menotropins 75 IU nightly. Start cetrorelix 0.25 mg daily today. Return June 10.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Right follicles 19, 18, 17, 16, 15, 13 mm; left 19, 18, 17, 16, 15, 13 mm. Endometrium 9.1 mm. Estradiol 6150 pmol/L, progesterone 2.3 nmol/L. Mild bloating, stable vital signs; no clinical OHSS.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Give final follitropin alfa 150 IU and menotropins 75 IU tonight. Continue cetrorelix through June 11. Leuprolide trigger tomorrow at 21:30 if no new concerns; egg retrieval June 13 at 09:30. Freeze-all strategy confirmed.

sections.heading: Telephone verification
sections.text: Patient administered final cetrorelix this morning and leuprolide acetate 4 mg SC at 21:30. Last gonadotropins taken June 10. Repeat-back confirmed retrieval June 13 at 09:30, 36 hours after trigger.

sections.heading: Instructions
sections.text: Fasting and escort instructions reviewed. No intercourse until recovered. Seek urgent assessment for severe pain, breathlessness, reduced urine or rapid abdominal swelling. No OHSS currently documented.

sections.heading: Pre-procedure
sections.text: SYN-IVF-01. Two identifiers and consent checked. Trigger June 11 at 21:30; procedure June 13 at 09:30. Afebrile, BP 114/72, pulse 74/min, SpO2 99%. No drug allergies.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text: Ultrasound-guided bilateral follicle aspiration under monitored IV sedation and local analgesia. Start 09:30, end 09:48. Twelve oocytes recovered and handed to embryologist Ari Quill. Estimated blood loss 10 mL; no complication.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.text: BP 110/68, pulse 70/min, SpO2 99%; alert, mild cramps, no active bleeding. Discharged with escort at 11:15. Fertilization assessment pending; mature-oocyte and blastocyst counts are not yet known.

sections.heading: Aftercare
sections.text: Rest today; acetaminophen if needed within labelled limits. Call for fever, heavy bleeding, increasing pain, vomiting or breathlessness. Embryology will call tomorrow.

sections.heading: Laboratory record
sections.text: SYN-IVF-01, retrieval June 13. Twelve oocytes retrieved; ten mature (MII), two immature (one MI, one GV). Ten mature oocytes underwent conventional IVF. Eight show normal 2PN fertilization at day-1 assessment; two mature oocytes did not fertilize.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue culture of eight normally fertilized embryos. Blastocyst number and cryopreservation outcome remain pending. No PGT requested.

sections.heading: Cycle outcome
sections.text: SYN-IVF-01: 12 retrieved, 10 mature, 8 normally fertilized. Four blastocysts cryopreserved in total. Embryos E01 and E02 vitrified on day 5 (June 18); E03 and E04 on day 6 (June 19). Four other 2PN embryos arrested and were not suitable for freezing under the laboratory policy.

sections.heading: Storage
sections.text: Embryos SYN-E01 to SYN-E04 each stored on an individually labelled device. No embryos transferred in this cycle. PGT not performed; morphology does not confirm chromosomal status. Witnesses Ari Quill and Rena Elm.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Four embryos remain stored. Review after recovery to plan a single frozen transfer.

documents.title: Final embryo culture and cryopreservation report

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Bloating resolved; withdrawal bleed began June 20 and ended June 24. No fever, severe pain or breathing symptoms.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Uncomplicated recovery. No OHSS diagnosed. Final laboratory outcome June 19: 12 retrieved, 10 mature, 8 2PN, 4 blastocysts frozen.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Patient chooses a treatment break before November frozen transfer. No further stimulation planned. Continue folic acid; discuss transfer preparation at October review.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Programmed single frozen transfer of day-5 embryo SYN-E01, subject to lining and pregnancy-test clearance. Last spontaneous bleeding October 27 is expected based on tracking; actual start must be confirmed before estradiol. No medication begins today.

sections.heading: Orders
sections.text: Estradiol 2 mg orally three times daily from cycle day 3 after confirmed bleed, quantity 204 tablets, no repeats. Progesterone in oil 50 mg IM daily at 09:00 from November 10 only after clearance, quantity 60 daily doses, no repeats. Continue through January 4 if pregnancy confirmed; otherwise stop only after clinic review.

sections.heading: Supplement
sections.text: Replace folic acid-only supplement with prenatal multivitamin containing folic acid 1 mg and iron 27 mg on November 1. Review IM injection training, medication allergies and pregnancy-test plan.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Menstrual bleeding began October 27, cycle day 3 today. Serum beta-hCG <1 IU/L. No interval illness.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Endometrium 3.4 mm; ovaries quiescent without cysts. Baseline estrogen 118 pmol/L.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Start estradiol 2 mg orally three times daily today. Return November 8 for lining assessment. Continue folic acid until switching to prenatal on November 1.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Endometrium 8.6 mm, trilaminar; no cavity fluid. Ovaries quiescent. Serum progesterone 0.8 nmol/L before supplementation.

sections.heading: Orders
sections.text: Continue estradiol 2 mg three times daily. Start progesterone in oil 50 mg IM daily November 10 at 09:00. Single day-5 embryo transfer planned November 15 at 09:00 after five completed days of progesterone. Pregnancy test November 25. Plans remain contingent on clinical status.

sections.heading: Identification and embryo
sections.text: SYN-FET-01. Two identifiers checked with patient and embryology witnesses Ari Quill and Rena Elm. SYN-E01, day-5 4AA blastocyst, frozen June 18, warmed today; survived with re-expansion. No PGT performed.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.text: At 09:00, ultrasound-guided atraumatic transfer of one embryo using soft catheter. Catheter check clear. No bleeding or complication. Three cryopreserved blastocysts remain: SYN-E02, SYN-E03 and SYN-E04.

sections.heading: Dating and plan
sections.text: Day-5 embryo transfer gives gestational age 2+5 today; ART-equivalent LMP October 27, 2024. If pregnancy established, EDD August 3, 2025. Pregnancy is not yet confirmed. Continue estradiol and progesterone; beta-hCG November 25. Routine activity as tolerated; urgent review for severe pain or heavy bleeding.

sections.heading: Interpretation
sections.text: Positive biochemical pregnancy test at 10 days after day-5 transfer. This value does not establish pregnancy location, viability or number. Repeat in 48 hours.

sections.heading: Interpretation
sections.text: Beta-hCG increased from 286 IU/L on November 25 to 642 IU/L today. Rise is compatible with early pregnancy; viability and location require ultrasound. Continue prescribed support pending clinic review.

sections.heading: Dating
sections.text: ART dating: day-5 transfer November 15; gestation 6+5; EDD August 3, 2025. Dating retained.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Single intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac and embryo. CRL 8.1 mm, approximately 6+5. Fetal cardiac activity 132/min. No subchorionic collection; no adnexal mass or free fluid.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: Single live intrauterine pregnancy, concordant with ART dates. Early scan cannot exclude all fetal anomalies.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue estradiol and progesterone through January 4, 2025 inclusive (9+6), stop January 5 at 10+0. Arrange obstetric intake and prenatal screening counselling.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: G1P0, gestation 10+1 by day-5 FET November 15. EDD August 3. Mild nausea without dehydration or bleeding. Estradiol and IM progesterone completed January 4 and stopped January 5 as instructed. Prenatal vitamin continues. No tobacco, alcohol or drug use in pregnancy.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: BP 108/66 mmHg, weight 62.0 kg, pulse 76/min; well hydrated.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Singleton IVF pregnancy confirmed on December 13 ultrasound. Initial prenatal laboratory panel ordered. Discuss options and limitations of aneuploidy screening; patient elects cfDNA and first-trimester ultrasound. Detailed anatomy scan to follow. Review infection precautions and urgent symptoms.

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: O positive; antibody screen negative. Rh immune globulin is not indicated for this RhD-positive patient. Rubella result supports immunity. No significant bacteriuria. Screening results reflect specimens collected January 6.

documents.specimen: Serum, EDTA blood, midstream urine and urine NAAT
documents.title: Initial prenatal laboratory panel

sections.heading: Specimen and pregnancy
sections.text: Maternal blood collected January 8 at 10+3. Singleton pregnancy following frozen embryo transfer; maternal age at EDD 32. Fetal fraction 9.2%; quality criteria met.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Low risk for trisomies 21, 18 and 13. Fetal sex not requested and not reported.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: This is screening, not diagnostic testing. It does not exclude all aneuploidy, structural anomalies or genetic disorders. Positive findings would require diagnostic confirmation; normal imaging remains separately assessed.

sections.heading: Dating
sections.text: ART gestation 12+5, EDD August 3, 2025. Transabdominal examination.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Single live fetus, CRL 64 mm, fetal heart rate 158/min. Nuchal translucency 1.6 mm. Nasal bone visualized. Limited early anatomy shows no major anomaly; posterior placenta. Ovaries without mass.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: Measurements concordant with ART dates; EDD retained. First-trimester assessment does not replace detailed anatomy survey.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Nausea improving; no bleeding or fluid loss. Mild constipation since starting prenatal vitamin; no abdominal tenderness.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 110/68, weight 63.0 kg, fetal heart rate 152/min by Doppler.

sections.heading: Review and plan
sections.text: January prenatal panel reassuring; cfDNA low risk, a screening result only. Discuss dietary fibre, fluids and activity for constipation. Anatomy ultrasound booked March 14. Continue prenatal vitamin.

sections.heading: Dating and technique
sections.text: Gestation 19+5 by ART; EDD August 3. Transabdominal detailed fetal survey.

sections.heading: Biometry
sections.text: BPD 46 mm; HC 170 mm; AC 148 mm; FL 31 mm. Estimated fetal weight 320 g, approximately 50th centile using synthetic local chart. Heart rate 148/min.

sections.heading: Anatomic survey
sections.text: Cranium, ventricles, posterior fossa, face, spine, situs, four-chamber heart, outflow tracts, stomach, abdominal wall, kidneys, bladder and limbs visualized without identified structural abnormality. Posterior placenta, lower edge 42 mm from internal os. Amniotic fluid normal. Cervix 36 mm transabdominally.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: Singleton with growth concordant with dates. No structural anomaly identified within scan limits. ART EDD retained; ultrasound cannot exclude every fetal condition.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Fetal movements present. No bleeding, fluid leakage, headache or visual symptoms. Occasional mechanical low-back ache after desk work.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 112/70, weight 65.2 kg, fundal height 23 cm, fetal heart rate 146/min.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Reviewed normal anatomy report. Discuss posture and gentle activity. Arrange 50 g glucose challenge and repeat CBC/ferritin at 26-28 weeks. Continue prenatal vitamin.

sections.heading: Context
sections.text: Nonfasting 50 g oral glucose challenge; specimen obtained one hour after dose. Result below 7.8 mmol/L screening threshold, no OGTT indicated by this result. Low ferritin and hemoglobin support iron deficiency with anemia in the second trimester.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Iron deficiency with anemia: hemoglobin 103 g/L, ferritin 9 ug/L on May 2 at 26+5.

sections.heading: Prescription
sections.text: Ferrous sulfate 300 mg tablet, 60 mg elemental iron orally every other day. Quantity 30 tablets, two repeats. Start May 5. Take separately from prenatal vitamin, calcium, tea and coffee; food if needed for nausea.

sections.heading: Follow-up
sections.text: Continue prenatal multivitamin. Repeat CBC/ferritin in June; escalate review if intolerance or failure to improve. This oral dose is a synthetic individual treatment order, not general medical advice.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: At 28+5, taking alternate-day iron with no nausea so far. Fetal movements usual. No contractions, bleeding or fluid loss.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 110/70, weight 67.0 kg, fundal height 28 cm, fetal heart rate 142/min.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Tdap vaccine administered with consent; no immediate reaction. Glucose screen negative. RhD positive; no routine Rh immune globulin. Continue iron and prenatal vitamin. Repeat hematology scheduled June 13.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.text: Hemoglobin improved from 103 to 112 g/L and ferritin from 9 to 22 ug/L after oral iron. Continue prescribed supplementation pending clinical review.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: IVF pregnancy growth assessment, 32+5 by ART, EDD August 3. Transabdominal examination.

sections.heading: Biometry
sections.text: BPD 82 mm; HC 296 mm; AC 286 mm; FL 63 mm. Estimated fetal weight 2040 g, approximately 40th centile on synthetic local chart. Fetal heart rate 140/min.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Cephalic singleton, posterior placenta without previa. Amniotic fluid index 13.2 cm. Fetal movements and tone observed.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text: Growth within expected range, no interval concern. EDD retained. Centiles are synthetic local reporting values and are not independently calculated chart outputs.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: No new symptoms; normal fetal movements. Mild dependent ankle swelling resolves overnight, no headache or visual change.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 114/72, weight 69.0 kg, fundal height 34 cm, fetal heart rate 140/min. No unilateral calf findings.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: June 13 hemoglobin 112 g/L and ferritin 22 ug/L improved; continue iron. Growth assessment reassuring. Discuss labour assessment and decreased fetal movement precautions. GBS swab at 36-37 weeks.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: At 36+5, fetal movements usual, no fluid loss or bleeding. Occasional painless tightenings.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 116/72, fundal height 36 cm, cephalic presentation, fetal heart rate 138/min.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Vaginal-rectal swab collected for group B streptococcus culture; result pending. Discuss labour signs, delivery preferences and postpartum support. Continue iron and prenatal vitamin.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Group B streptococcus not isolated from vaginal-rectal swab collected July 11. Result applies to this collection; intrapartum decisions also depend on risk factors.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Normal movements, intermittent Braxton Hicks tightenings. No bleeding, fluid loss, persistent headache or visual symptoms.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 114/70, fundal height 38 cm, fetal heart rate 136/min, cephalic.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: GBS culture July 13 negative. Discussed expectant care and induction options around 39-40 weeks for IVF pregnancy. Patient prefers spontaneous labour for now; next review July 31 if undelivered. Continue prescribed supplements.

sections.heading: Admission
sections.text: Admitted July 29 at 02:10 with regular painful contractions, G1P0 at 39+2 by ART, EDD August 3. Cervix 5 cm/90%/-1. Membranes initially intact. BP 118/74, afebrile. O positive, antibody negative, GBS July 13 not isolated.

sections.heading: Labour course
sections.text: Epidural placed at 04:05 without documented complication. Spontaneous rupture of membranes at 06:20, clear fluid. Continuous fetal monitoring reassuring. Full dilation 10:50; spontaneous vaginal delivery at 11:42.

sections.heading: Birth
sections.text: Live singleton female newborn, ID SYN-INFANT-001, weight 3320 g. Apgar scores 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. Placenta delivered intact at 11:49; three-vessel cord. Second-degree perineal tear repaired. Quantified blood loss 350 mL. Oxytocin 10 IU IM after delivery at 11:45.

sections.heading: Immediate postpartum
sections.text: Mother stable, uterus firm, normal lochia. Skin-to-skin and breastfeeding initiated. No postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorder or neonatal resuscitation beyond routine care documented. G1P1 following birth.

laboratory_values.reference_context: nonpregnant laboratory interval; interpret early postpartum

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Collected on postpartum day 1. Mild anemia following delivery; stable clinically with no ongoing heavy bleeding. Compare pregnancy hemoglobin 112 g/L on June 13.

sections.heading: Admission and discharge
sections.text: Admission July 29, discharge July 31. Term IVF singleton pregnancy delivered at 39+2 on July 29 at 11:42. Spontaneous vaginal delivery; second-degree tear repaired. QBL 350 mL. Infant SYN-INFANT-001 female, 3320 g, Apgar 8/9.

sections.heading: Hospital course
sections.text: Afebrile, normotensive, ambulating and voiding normally. Uterus firm and bleeding appropriate. Breastfeeding with positioning support. July 30 hemoglobin 106 g/L. No postpartum hemorrhage or infection diagnosed.

sections.heading: Discharge medications
sections.text: Continue prenatal vitamin daily and ferrous sulfate 300 mg every other day. Ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours as needed, maximum 1200 mg/day, and acetaminophen 500-1000 mg every 8 hours as needed, maximum 3000 mg/day; seven-day supply, no repeats.

sections.heading: Follow-up
sections.text: Nurse call August 5 and postpartum examination September 9. Pelvic rest until comfortable and healing assessed. Seek urgent care for soaking a pad hourly, fever, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, unilateral leg swelling or thoughts of self-harm. Contraception discussed; condoms planned when intercourse resumes. Copy to Dr Elara Vale.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Postpartum day 7. Lochia decreasing, no fever or heavy bleeding. Perineal pain improving; stopped ibuprofen and acetaminophen August 3. Breastfeeding established with occasional nipple tenderness; no red hot breast or systemic symptoms. Sleep fragmented but support available.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Review latch support and urgent symptoms. Continue prenatal vitamin and alternate-day iron. No depressive disorder diagnosed on this call. In-person review September 9.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: 42 days after July 29 birth. G1P1. Breastfeeding, no menses since delivery. Lochia ended August 23. Mild urine leakage with cough; no dysuria, retention or prolapse symptoms. Uses condoms; pregnancy spacing discussed.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: BP 110/68, weight 63.8 kg. Perineal repair healed. No uterine tenderness. EPDS 4/30, self-harm item 0; no depression diagnosis.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Refer pelvic health physiotherapy for stress leakage. Continue iron and prenatal vitamin while breastfeeding. Repeat CBC/ferritin in October. Cervical screening due under updated HPV programme; patient elects to defer collection until January 2026 after counselling.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Small leakage with coughing and jogging since birth. No urgency, dysuria, hematuria or pelvic pain. Breastfeeding; no menstrual return yet.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: Consent and chaperone option documented. Pelvic floor contraction 3/5 with reduced endurance and delayed pre-cough contraction. Healed perineum; no significant prolapse observed.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Postpartum stress urinary incontinence. Teach coordinated pelvic floor contraction, breathing and graded return to exercise. Home practice 8 contractions held up to 6 seconds twice daily as tolerated. Reassess in November; stop if pain occurs.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.text: Hemoglobin 125 g/L and ferritin 42 ug/L have recovered from postpartum hemoglobin 106 g/L on July 30. Review treatment duration with primary care.

sections.heading: Subjective
sections.text: Rare leakage only with repeated cough; no leakage during walking or gentle exercise. Home practice comfortable. No urinary infection symptoms.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Improved pelvic floor coordination and endurance. Continue exercises and gradual activity. Follow up as needed; no medication or surgical treatment indicated.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Breastfeeding; infant currently four months old. Infant feeding guidance remains with the infant care team. No menstrual bleeding yet. No fatigue, urinary leakage now rare. Therapeutic iron tolerated.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: October 10 hemoglobin 125 g/L, ferritin 42 ug/L; resolved postpartum anemia. Continue diet after completed replenishment.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Last therapeutic iron dose today; stop December 6. Continue prenatal vitamin while breastfeeding. January cervical-screening visit confirmed. No additional embryo transfer planned; three embryos remain stored per fertility record.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: First postpartum menstrual period began January 12, ended January 16; light to moderate flow. No postcoital or intermenstrual bleeding. Breastfeeding reduced; plans to wean by end of January. No further fertility treatment planned. Condoms for contraception.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: BP 112/70, weight 61.8 kg. Speculum examination with consent and chaperone Rena Elm: cervix normal, no abnormal discharge or contact bleeding. HPV screening sample collected.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Primary HPV screening under Ontario programme introduced in 2025; previous February 2022 cytology NILM. Result pending. Finish prenatal vitamin January 31 after weaning; no other regular medication. Continue tracking natural cycles.

documents.title: Routine care and HPV screening collection

sections.heading: Specimen
sections.text: Clinician-collected cervical liquid-based sample, collected January 16. Valid assay controls.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: High-risk HPV not detected, including HPV 16, HPV 18 and pooled other high-risk types. Reflex cytology not indicated following HPV-negative primary screen.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.text: Average-risk routine recall in five years, January 2031, under current Ontario screening guidance. Symptoms require separate assessment regardless of negative screening.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Weaned January 31. Menstrual starts January 12, February 15 and March 19: intervals 34 and 32 days. Flow 4-5 days, moderate first two days, mild cramps. No abnormal bleeding or pelvic pain. Condoms used. No desire for pregnancy this year.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Early postpartum cycle variability documented without a diagnosis of PCOS or anovulation. HPV January 21 negative, next routine recall 2031. No regular medications. Continue tracking; review for prolonged amenorrhea, heavy bleeding or pregnancy concern.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Mild recurrent fatigue since returning to work. Natural cycles now 29-32 days, 4-5 bleeding days. No heavy bleeding, GI symptoms, weight loss or breathlessness. Mostly vegetarian diet; no therapeutic iron since December.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: BP 110/70, weight 61.5 kg, pulse 72/min. Examination unremarkable.

sections.heading: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Recurrent iron deficiency suspected; request CBC, ferritin and TSH. Sleep interruption may contribute; avoid diagnosing anemia before results. No pregnancy symptoms, contraception with condoms.

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Ferritin below range with hemoglobin within adult female range. Findings support recurrent iron deficiency without anemia. TSH normal.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: June 15 ferritin 13 ug/L and hemoglobin 122 g/L confirm iron deficiency without anemia. No evidence supplied for thyroid disease or major blood loss.

sections.heading: Prescription
sections.text: Ferrous sulfate 300 mg tablet, providing 60 mg elemental iron, orally every other day. Quantity 45 tablets, one repeat. Evening with food if nausea. Start today; repeat CBC/ferritin in September.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Review dietary intake. Investigate further if no response, heavy bleeding or GI symptoms. Keep medication apart from calcium, tea and coffee.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.text: Ferritin increased from 13 ug/L on June 15 to 35 ug/L; hemoglobin from 122 to 129 g/L. Treatment response documented.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Fatigue improved. Oral iron tolerated. Cycles now 28-31 days with moderate flow. No new bleeding or GI symptoms. Urinary leakage resolved with exercises.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: September 18 hemoglobin 129 g/L and ferritin 35 ug/L. HPV screen negative January 2026. Three blastocysts remain stored; no subsequent transfer or pregnancy documented.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue alternate-day iron through December 18 to replenish stores, then reassess. Influenza vaccination offered and accepted. Continue condoms and cycle tracking.

sections.heading: Comment
sections.text: Iron indices remain improved during replacement. Compare September 18 hemoglobin 129 g/L and ferritin 35 ug/L.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Well, regular natural cycles, no fatigue or urinary leakage. G1P1 after single IVF pregnancy and July 29, 2025 vaginal birth. Uses condoms; no current conception attempts. Child well by patient report; this is not an infant medical chart.

sections.heading: Examination
sections.text: BP 112/68, weight 61.4 kg. No abnormal cardiopulmonary or abdominal findings.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: December 11 hemoglobin 131 g/L, ferritin 48 ug/L. Recurrent iron deficiency improved; complete last iron dose today and stop December 19. HPV negative January 2026, routine recall January 2031. No evidence of PCOS, endometriosis, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disease or postpartum depression.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.text: Continue dietary iron and routine care. Repeat iron studies if symptoms or bleeding recur. Three cryopreserved embryos remain from the single 2024 retrieval; no further treatment scheduled.
